result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.minimum_spanning_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the minimum spanning tree using Kruskal's algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22671-L22773){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.minimum_spanning_tree( weight_attr=None, return_subgraph=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A minimum spanning tree (MST) is a subset of edges that connects all nodes with the minimum total edge weight. Uses the optimized union-find data structure with path-halving for efficient cycle detection. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of edge attribute to use for weights. If `None` (the default), uses the edge's weight field. If the attribute doesn't exist on an edge, defaults to `1.0`. [return_subgraph]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a new Graph containing only the MST edges. If `False`, returns a list of edge IDs as strings. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph or list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Either a new Graph with MST edges or a list of edge ID strings, depending on the `return_subgraph=` parameter. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(E log E)` for sorting edges - space complexity: `O(V)` for union-find structure - for disconnected graphs, finds a minimum spanning forest - if graph has < 2 nodes, returns empty graph or list ## Examples {.doc-examples} This 4-cycle plus one diagonal has 5 edges total, but connecting all 4 nodes only requires 3 of them -- the MST keeps the 3 cheapest edges that avoid forming a cycle: ::: {#98ab9423 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(weighted=True) g.add_node("A") g.add_node("B") g.add_node("C") g.add_node("D") g.add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.0) g.add_edge("B", "C", weight=2.0) g.add_edge("C", "D", weight=3.0) g.add_edge("D", "A", weight=4.0) g.add_edge("A", "C", weight=5.0) mst = g.minimum_spanning_tree() # Returns 3 (connects all 4 nodes with the minimum number of edges) mst.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#81b8e706 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Calculate total weight of the tree total = sum( e.weight for e in [mst.get_edge(eid) for eid, _, _ in mst.get_edges_as_tuples()] if e and e.weight is not None ) # Returns 6.0 (edges A-B, B-C, C-D, skipping the two priciest edges) total ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 6.0 ``` ::: :::
